findings.requirement: Preserve the native recursive_triggers setting observed by user SQL. Audit failures must propagate and roll back the transfer; harmless guards must continue to succeed.
findings.evidence: Initialize a temporary database and seed accounts ('red','a',100), ('red','b',20). Install: CREATE VIEW saved_mode AS SELECT recursive_triggers FROM (pragma_recursive_triggers()); CREATE TRIGGER native_guard BEFORE INSERT ON audit WHEN (SELECT recursive_triggers FROM saved_mode)=0 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'native guard'); END; Call transfer(path,'red','a','b',10,'new'). The .pre-repair implementation raises IntegrityError and preserves all rows. The candidate returns success and commits balances 90/30, a receipt and an audit row. Changing the guard comparison to =1 reverses the regression: .pre-repair succeeds, while the candidate aborts. The rewriter misses the parenthesized table source, exposing its forced recursive_triggers=1. Additional probes demonstrated incorrect CTE shadow resolution and broken schema-qualified column references in the same rewriting mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve native pragma visibility and SQLite name resolution throughout instrumentation, including parenthesized sources, scoped CTEs and qualified references. Verify both aborting and harmless controls.
findings.additional_reproduction: CREATE VIEW saved_mode AS WITH pragma_recursive_triggers(recursive_triggers) AS (VALUES(7)) SELECT * FROM pragma_recursive_triggers; guard BEFORE INSERT ON audit WHEN (SELECT recursive_triggers FROM saved_mode)<>7 must succeed; =7 must abort. Current rewrites reverse these. Also CREATE VIEW saved_mode AS SELECT main.pragma_recursive_triggers.recursive_triggers FROM main.pragma_recursive_triggers(); with harmless <>0 guard currently raises no such column. Both native controls pass and latest baseline round 3 passes all four native/API/CLI comparisons. Keep quoted and parenthesized table sources, scalar expressions and exact restored SQL valid. Historical view INSTEAD OF INSERT triggers must remain functional.

findings.requirement: Preserve nested RAISE(IGNORE) scope and existing trigger behavior. Storage/audit failures must propagate without committing transfer effects.
findings.evidence: Seed accounts ('red','a',100), ('red','b',20), ('blue','p',77), ('blue','q',88), in that order. Install: CREATE TRIGGER guard BEFORE UPDATE ON accounts WHEN OLD.tenant='blue' BEGIN SELECT CASE WHEN OLD.name='p' THEN RAISE(IGNORE) ELSE RAISE(ABORT,'native guard') END; END; CREATE TRIGGER effect AFTER INSERT ON audit BEGIN UPDATE accounts SET balance=balance WHERE tenant='blue'; END; Call transfer(path,'red','a','b',10,'new'). The .pre-repair implementation raises IntegrityError on q and rolls everything back. The candidate returns success and commits balances 90/30, the receipt and audit. RAISE(IGNORE) leaves guard's synthetic frame active, so _allowed suppresses its invocation for the next row. Replacing THEN RAISE(IGNORE) with THEN 0 makes both implementations correctly abort, confirming the cause.
findings.suggested_fix: Unwind abandoned trigger frames before subsequent row invocations within the same statement. Cleanup only at the next parent statement is insufficient. Cover multirow nested IGNORE with both aborting and harmless controls.
findings.additional_regression: Historical multirow IGNORE tests fail for BEFORE and AFTER, including conditional mixed-case RaIsE /*comment*/( IgNoRe ) with an earlier self-noop statement and later changes()/total_changes() guards. A scratch table with rows 1,2,3 and a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that logs OLD.n then RAISE(IGNORE) should log each affected row; current records only first. Parent trigger must resume after the UPDATE. Preserve explicit DELETE user triggers but not invoke them for native implicit REPLACE victims when native recursive_triggers=0.
